scope: Proposition 5.3 (Matching of the transports) of the manuscript “Global Uniqueness for the Smooth Isotropic Elasticity Inverse Problem” (preprints/Global-Uniqueness-for-the-Smooth-Isotropic-Elasticity-Inverse-Problem-September-24-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 372 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5cadfeb6eb45bea2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the two extended coefficient pairs of Lemma 2.1, equality of the physical displacement-to-traction maps implies that there is a unique smooth field G(x, [θ]) ∈ End(Eθ), (x, [θ]) ∈ R3 × C, satisfying, for every nonzero representative θ, DθG = M2,θG − GM1,θ, G(x, [θ]) = Id if |x| > 2r. (5.10) For each fixed x, this field is a holomorphic section of End(E) over C. In fact, for each fixed direction the first equation has at most one smooth solution whose difference from the identity has compact spatial support.
